newsitem.title: CHINA: Tobacco firm to back clean air talk at China forum.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco firm to back clean air talk at China forum.

text.p: China will next month hold a four-day conference on the environment that will aim to unite government officials, experts and businessmen in the cause of sustainable development, conference officials said on Tuesday.

The 1997 China Environment Forum would include a series of panel discussions sponsored by international companies, with the discussion on Indoor Air Quality to be backed by tobacco giant B.A.T Industries, the officials said.

The forum, to be organised by two officially approved Chinese environmental organisations and endorsed by the National Environmental Protection Agency, aimed to apply international development experience and boost global cooperation, they said.

"The environment is an issue that involves everybody," Ye Ruqiu, of the Chinese Society for Environmental Sciences, told a reception of journalists, organisers and prospective participants of the February 24-27 conference.

Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng were expected to attend the forum, along with international participants, such as former Norwegian prime minister Gro Harlem Brundtland, organisers said.

Apart from indoor air quality, other economic sectors identified as high priorities for enhanced environmental management included electric power, the chemical industry, tourism and defence, they said.
